q: A teammate's lab environment cost $35 last month even though nothing was running. The VPC has public and private subnets in two AZs, one NAT gateway, no EC2 instances. What is the most likely cause?
options: The NAT gateway, which bills per hour whether or not traffic flows
The private route tables
The internet gateway
The VPC itself is billed hourly
explain: VPCs, subnets, route tables and internet gateways are free. A NAT gateway costs roughly $0.045/hour (about $33/month) plus per-GB processing, even when idle, and its Elastic IP adds a public IPv4 charge.

q: Which is the recommended way for you, as a human, to give Terraform AWS credentials on your Mac?
options: Root account credentials, because they never expire
An IAM Identity Center profile created with `aws configure sso`, refreshed with `aws sso login` and selected with `AWS_PROFILE`
`access_key` and `secret_key` in the provider block, read from `terraform.tfvars`
An IAM user access key stored in `~/.aws/credentials`
explain: IAM Identity Center issues short-lived credentials after a browser login; nothing long-lived sits on disk or in code. Static IAM user keys leak and never expire on their own, and root credentials should never be used for daily work.

q: What does `default_tags` in the AWS provider block give you? (select all)
options: Automatic tags on resources created by a different provider alias without its own `default_tags`
Encryption of the resources' data
A consistent way to find Terraform-managed resources in Tag Editor and Cost Explorer
Tags merged into every taggable resource created through that provider block
explain: `default_tags` applies per provider block, so an alias needs its own `default_tags`. Tags are metadata used for ownership, cost allocation and finding leftovers; they have nothing to do with encryption.
Adding 8 bits to a /16 gives /24 networks; netnum 10 selects the eleventh /24, which is `10.0.10.0/24`.

q: What makes a subnet "public" in AWS?
options: Its associated route table has a route for `0.0.0.0/0` to an internet gateway
It is in the first availability zone
It has a security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0
Setting `map_public_ip_on_launch = true`
explain: Public means routable to the internet through an IGW. `map_public_ip_on_launch` only auto-assigns public IPs; without the IGW route those IPs are useless. Security groups are per-interface firewalls, not subnet properties.

q: Your Fargate service runs in private subnets with no NAT gateway and no VPC endpoints. Tasks keep stopping with `ResourceInitializationError ... i/o timeout`. What is wrong?
options: The tasks have no network path to the container registry, so the image pull times out
The CPU architecture is wrong
Fargate does not support private subnets
The task role lacks `s3:GetObject`
explain: Pulling images and sending logs needs outbound access: a NAT gateway, or VPC endpoints for ECR API, ECR DKR, S3 (gateway) and CloudWatch Logs. A wrong architecture shows as `exec format error` after the pull succeeds.

q: In ECS, which role does the ECS agent use to pull a private ECR image and write logs to CloudWatch?
options: The service-linked role for Auto Scaling
The task execution role
The task role
The EC2 instance profile
explain: The task execution role is used by ECS itself (image pull, logs, secrets injection). The task role is what your application code uses to call AWS APIs.

q: Which settings belong to a hardened S3 bucket in Terraform with AWS provider v4 or later? (select all)
options: `aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls` with `BucketOwnerEnforced`
A bucket policy denying requests where `aws:SecureTransport` is false
`aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` with all four options true
A `versioning {}` block inside `aws_s3_bucket`
explain: Since provider v4 bucket settings are separate resources (`aws_s3_bucket_versioning`, `_server_side_encryption_configuration`, ...). The inline `versioning {}` block is the old style. Public access block, enforced ownership (ACLs off) and a TLS-only policy are standard hardening.

q: You create `aws_security_group.web` with only an ingress rule. Your Fargate task in a public subnet cannot pull its image. Why?
options: Terraform removes AWS's default allow-all egress rule, so the group has no outbound rule
Ingress rules must be inline blocks
Security groups are stateless, so responses are blocked
Public subnets cannot pull images
explain: AWS adds an allow-all egress rule to new groups, but the Terraform resource deletes it. You must declare egress explicitly, e.g. `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule` with `ip_protocol = "-1"`. Security groups are stateful.

q: You need an SNS topic in `us-east-1` for billing alarms while the rest of the stack is in `eu-central-1`, same account. With AWS provider v6, which options work? Choose the best description.
options: Set `AWS_REGION=us-east-1` for that resource only
Use `depends_on` on a us-east-1 data source
Only a second Terraform root module can do this
Either a provider alias with `region = "us-east-1"` referenced via `provider = aws.use1`, or the per-resource `region = "us-east-1"` argument
explain: Aliases have always solved multi-region; provider v6 added enhanced region support so most resources accept `region` directly. Aliases remain necessary for different credentials/accounts or passing providers into modules.

q: Why use `aws_iam_policy_document` instead of a heredoc JSON string for IAM policies?
options: It is the only way to attach a policy to a role
It renders valid JSON from HCL locally, supports interpolation and composition, and avoids JSON syntax and whitespace diffs
It enforces least privilege automatically
It creates a managed policy in AWS
explain: It is a data source computed locally (no API call) that outputs `.json`. You still attach it with `aws_iam_role_policy` or `aws_iam_policy`. It does not judge whether your permissions are minimal.

q: Which statements about LocalStack in 2026 are correct? (select all)
options: A successful apply against LocalStack does not prove the same config works on AWS
Every AWS service, including ECS and EKS, is emulated on the free plan
The free Hobby plan is for non-commercial use
It now requires an account and an auth token, even on the free plan
explain: Since 23 March 2026 a single image requires `LOCALSTACK_AUTH_TOKEN`; the free Hobby tier is non-commercial and covers a subset of services (ECS/ECR are paid at the time of writing). Emulation differs from AWS, and IAM is not enforced on the free plan.

q: When is writing your own VPC resources better than `terraform-aws-modules/vpc`?
options: When you want to avoid pinning versions
When you are learning, or need a small, very specific design whose every resource you want to review
Never; community modules are always better
When you need IPv6, flow logs and endpoints
explain: Writing it yourself teaches the parts and yields small plans. The community module is faster and feature-rich, and production teams often wrap it. Either way you pin versions; modules must always be pinned.
